site.title: ChatGPT Tips Watch
site.tagline: Searchable reference of ChatGPT and Codex tips from 16 accounts on X
site.scope_short: Codex, ChatGPT features, dots, OpenAI models and the OpenAI API
site.scope_about: ChatGPT and OpenAI tooling (Codex, ChatGPT features and dots, custom instructions, plugins, model choice, prompting and the OpenAI API)
site.scope_note: Only ChatGPT and OpenAI tooling is covered here. Tips about Claude or other AI tools are left out, even when they come from the same accounts; a tip about a tool that works with several agents is included only when it names ChatGPT, Codex or an OpenAI product.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Model stopping early? Raise reasoning effort first
tips.tip: For long-horizon work with GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra: if the model stops early, try increasing the reasoning effort before reaching for goal mode. Max effort isn't normally recommended, but it's worth trying when you want the model to work for hours.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Read the Codex prompting guide, not the API guide
tips.tip: The API prompt guide's advice is already built into Codex's system prompt. For best practices on working with GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol inside Codex, read the Codex-specific guide instead.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Report code-quality problems with /feedback
tips.tip: If you spot code-quality issues in GPT-written code (for example defensive "just in case" fallbacks that hide bugs), run `/feedback` and add a comment explaining what is wrong with it.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Keep network access separate from repo edits
tips.tip: A command that edits your repo shouldn't automatically get network access. The Codex sandbox runs commands in your existing environment within the filesystem and network limits you control.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Inside the Codex sandbox
tips.tip: OpenAI's write-up covers the tradeoffs behind Codex's sandbox defaults, how the harness uses the sandbox to run commands, how users and enterprises can tailor its permissions, how developers can reuse the sandbox in their own tools, and how it is enforced on macOS, Linux and Windows.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: SVG & 3D Design plugin for Codex
tips.tip: The SVG & 3D Design plugin for Codex guides Astra to ask GPT Image for a reference suited to the medium, refine it and use it as concept art, for anything from editable app icons to parametric CAD. For vector graphics, it has Sol and Astra generate references with details that convert well to curves and gradients in code.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Guide 3D work with an image reference
tips.tip: GPT-6.2 Astra is especially strong at 3D graphics when an image reference guides it; the demo runs in a desktop browser with WebGPU.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Pair Astra with gpt-image-2.6 for slides
tips.tip: Astra's slide typography and layouts feel more intentional, especially when you pair it with `gpt-image-2.6`.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Richer SVGs with GPT Image 2.6
tips.tip: When Astra 6.2 uses GPT Image 2.6, it can produce detailed SVGs (example: an otter riding a bicycle in Japan at 291 KB).

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: How a 1:1 Singapore was built
tips.tip: A 1:1-scale Singapore (200,000+ building footprints, 160,000+ road segments, 120,000+ streetlights) took 100+ Astra Codex threads, 1,000+ subagents and over 100 hours of work.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Let a dot coordinate many Codex threads
tips.tip: His dot coordinated the 100+ GPT-6.2 Astra threads over the 100+ hours of the Singapore build.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: OpenAI's Performance Factory pattern
tips.tip: OpenAI built a Codex-powered Performance Factory that coordinates agents to investigate performance regressions, propose fixes for engineers to review, and check whether those fixes work in production.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Pin Codex in the new mobile app
tips.tip: In the new ChatGPT mobile experience, pin Codex to the tab bar for quick access.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Give your dot custom instructions
tips.tip: Dots now follow custom instructions. Tell your dot in the thread how to behave or which actions need your go-ahead (for example "always talk in lowercase" or "Show me a draft before sending any emails"), or set instructions and rules in Customize > Behavior on mobile or from your dot's menu on web and desktop.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Your dot's own email address (testing)
tips.tip: Dots are getting their own email address (testing has started): cc your dot and ask it to "find a time that works for everyone", or forward it a receipt and ask it to help negotiate a refund, without leaving your inbox.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Send your dot a reference photo to edit video remotely
tips.tip: He sends an edited photo to his dot, and it color-grades and edits a video on his laptop at the other end of the country.

tips.author: thsottiaux
tips.title: Try the new ChatGPT mobile design
tips.tip: A new ChatGPT mobile experience is rolling out to Pro users who have (or can create) a dot: the dot gets its own tab, and you can pin Codex, Projects, Images and more to the tab bar. Turn it on or off in Settings > New ChatGPT Design.

tips.author: thsottiaux
tips.title: Dots are expanding to Plus and Business
tips.tip: Dots are being tested with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users, and rolling out to all ChatGPT Business Standard users.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Live Dictation
tips.tip: With Live Dictation, ChatGPT turns your speech into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for a message to finish transcribing.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Let your dot pay with ChatGPT Wallet
tips.tip: Your dot can complete purchases for you, with your approval. With ChatGPT Wallet, agents pay without access to your actual card details and every purchase requires a security check. Rolling out to dots for Pro subscribers in the US.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: ChatGPT for Sales plugins
tips.tip: ChatGPT for Sales combines a new Sales plugin with 30+ new and enhanced partner plugins, so ChatGPT can use your sales tools and customer context.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: What the Sales plugin is for
tips.tip: The Sales plugin includes dedicated skills for sellers, and partner plugins pull in information from the tools your team already uses to prepare for calls, tailor proposals and follow up faster.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: ChatGPT for Accounting plugins
tips.tip: The Accounting plugin and partner plugins help with month-end reports, bank reconciliation, data entry and audit prep, working with tools like QuickBooks, Xero, Oracle NetSuite, BILL, FreshBooks, Rillet and Campfire.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Use Health across desktop, dots and Sites
tips.tip: With connected health data, ChatGPT can analyze sleep and workout patterns on desktop, your dot can suggest another workout time when a meeting gets in the way, you can build a Site to track marathon training, and Android Health Connect brings in sleep, activity and workouts. Health is available in the U.S. on desktop and Android for Free, Go, Plus and Pro; Sites need Plus or Pro, and dots need Pro.

tips.author: reach_vb
tips.title: Astra for the hardest work, Sol for cost
tips.tip: Use GPT-6.2 Astra for your hardest projects and Sol for strong results at a fraction of the cost: on FrontierCode 2.0, Sol nearly matches Astra on merge-ready changes to real codebases at about one-fifth the cost. API pricing per 1M tokens: Astra $8 input / $0.40 cached / $40 output; Sol $2 / $0.10 / $10.

tips.author: OpenAI
tips.title: Where 6.2 is available, and Ultrafast
tips.tip: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu. Pro 500 can use Ultrafast with either model; Pro 200 gets Ultrafast with Sol. In the API they are gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, with Ultrafast available.

tips.author: thsottiaux
tips.title: Sol as the day-to-day default
tips.tip: GPT-6.2 Sol is his go-to model for most day-to-day things, and Ultrafast now covers Sol on Pro 200 plans.

tips.author: reach_vb
tips.title: Give a new model a few varied tasks
tips.tip: Spend time with 6.2 Astra and Sol on a variety of tasks; like any new model it takes some getting used to. He has delegated many of his existing workflows to it.

tips.author: danshipper
tips.title: Every's early read on Astra 6.2
tips.tip: Every's testing found Astra 6.2 a step back on writing (very concise, sometimes too short), similar to Astra 6 on coding benchmarks but prone to stopping too early on real end-to-end builds, and good at default design but with a noticeable "house style".

tips.author: danshipper
tips.title: Full Every vibe check
tips.tip: Every's full ratings for Astra and Sol 6.2 are in its vibe check.

tips.author: simonw
tips.title: Same prompt, Astra vs Sol
tips.tip: Simon Willison ran the same three.js prompt (a mech stomping around New York using OpenStreetMap data) on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol and wrote up the results.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Background mode discounts for work that can wait
tips.tip: For single- or multi-turn workflows that can wait, Responses API background mode lets you pick a 2h or 8h target for the first response and save up to 40% per token versus Standard on GPT-6.2 Astra or Sol (public beta).

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Reasoning items are tied to history
tips.tip: With GPT-6.2 in the Responses API, each reasoning item is tied to the conversation history before it, so agents can build on earlier reasoning with fewer tokens and more cache hits. Editing an earlier message makes the API drop the reasoning that follows the change.

tips.author: steipete
tips.title: Instructions-field caching bug on 6.2
tips.tip: A reported bug (Codex issue #62312): on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, content in the top-level `instructions` field of a Responses API request isn't cached, even though diagnostics report a cache hit; one report saw cache hit rates fall from 97.4% to 46.4%. Workaround: put the system prompt in a leading developer message in `input`. He landed a fix in OpenClaw's embedded harness.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Investigate usage in the Analytics dashboard
tips.tip: The API usage dashboard's Analytics view now tracks usage and spend, shows rate limits and rate-limited requests, and lets you explore errors by model, project or API key.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: GPT-Live-1.1 standby option
tips.tip: GPT-Live-1.1 in the API speaks with more natural, consistent accents across languages, completes tasks more reliably, and has a new standby option for lower idle costs.

tips.author: kevins8
tips.title: Manage persistent agents like contractors
tips.tip: Persistent agents like OpenClaw or dots act more like contractors than SaaS: they take proactive actions in the background and can take misaligned actions or write code with unintended consequences. OpenAI published the practices it uses to manage fleets of them internally.

tips.author: simonw
tips.title: The external sandbox pattern
tips.tip: In the external sandbox pattern, the coding agent runs on your Mac but executes code inside a WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandbox. The write-up includes a demo for Codex (plus Claude Code and Pi).

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Daybreak Defense Factory
tips.tip: Daybreak Defense Factory scans code in a connected GitHub repository and shares the findings with your team.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Where dot custom instructions live on desktop
tips.tip: On desktop, open the three-dot menu on the dot sidebar and choose Custom instructions (the same menu has Rename, Pause, Reboot and Delete).

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Write instructions as plain-language rules
tips.tip: Type rules in plain language, such as when and where to notify you (the demo asks to be told in Slack about urgent updates), then Save.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Pick a completion window
tips.tip: Background Mode offers completion windows from Ultrafast, Fast and Standard to 2h and 8h; the longer windows are the discounted ones.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Request shape for an 8h window
tips.tip: Set `"background": true` and `"background_options": {"completion_window": "8h"}` on the request (shown with `gpt-6.2-sol`). Good for jobs like overnight morning briefs.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Keep a human deciding what ships
tips.tip: In the Performance Factory loop, agents find the root cause and propose a fix, but an engineer reviews and deploys it.

tips.author: OpenAIDevs
tips.title: Have the agent verify recovery
tips.tip: After deployment, the agent checks whether performance recovered; if it is still regressed, the loop goes back to investigation instead of closing.

tips.author: thsottiaux
tips.title: Find modules behind the grid icon
tips.tip: The grid icon at the bottom right of the tab bar opens modules such as Projects, Images, Scheduled, Codex, Plugins, Health and Sites.

tips.author: thsottiaux
tips.title: Pin a module to the tab bar
tips.tip: Tap and hold a module (for example Codex) and choose Pin to tab bar, or Reorder.

tips.author: thsottiaux
tips.title: Connect apps from the dot chat
tips.tip: Your dot can offer integrations right in the chat, such as a Connect button for Gmail.

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Publish a Site from one detailed Codex prompt
tips.tip: Point Codex at existing data (a Google Sheet in the demo) and describe the whole app in one prompt: the design system to use, what must be visible on the first screen, filters, views (list, board, calendar) and links to open. The demo prompt: "Can you turn this sheet into a launch radar app in a new folder and then publish it as a site?" followed by those requirements. The result includes a built-in SQLite database.

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Keep a Site's data fresh with a scheduled task
tips.tip: Ask Codex to set up a recurring refresh, for example "Can you keep this site up-to-date every morning using the launch briefs linked from the sheet." It creates a scheduled task (shown later as Repeat: Daily, 8:00 AM).

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Sites are private by default
tips.tip: Sites come with Sign in with ChatGPT and start restricted. Use the "Who can access" menu to choose Only you, Specific people, Your organization or Public.

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Add a read/write connector so each user sees their own data
tips.tip: Ask Codex to add a connector to the site with read and write access (Linear in the demo) so each signed-in person sees their own assigned tickets and can change a status or description and save it back.

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Give a teammate Editor access
tips.tip: Click Share, add the person, and set their permission to Editor so they can make structural changes to the site.

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Edit visually with Annotation mode
tips.tip: Click the Annotate button and allow annotation mode when the site asks. Then click a UI component, adjust it with the on-screen controls, and confirm the change in the Codex chat to apply it.

tips.author: kagigz
tips.title: Expose site tools to agents with WebMCP
tips.tip: WebMCP is a browser standard that lets an agent call a site's tools directly instead of clicking through the UI. In the demo the agent opens the site's "Available site tools" and uses a "Suggest items" tool to answer a gift request built from Slack DMs.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Iterate on UI with Ultrafast instead of one long task
tips.tip: When you don't yet know exactly what a UI should look like, start with a rough direction, get something on screen fast, and react to what Codex builds with small rounds of feedback. With Ultrafast each change often takes only a couple of seconds, so you stay in the zone instead of waiting on a long high-reasoning task.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Set up the fast loop: hot reload + in-app browser
tips.tip: Run a dev server with hot module reloading so changes show up as soon as Codex makes them, and keep the site open in the in-app browser next to the chat so you see results while you prompt.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Short tasks, annotations and dictation
tips.tip: Send one small piece of feedback at a time. Use annotations to point at the exact element you want changed instead of describing where it is, and use dictation or voice mode to queue several small tasks while you keep looking at the result. A keyboard shortcut for dictation (or a Codex Micro) makes queuing feedback while scrolling a page quick.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Start at Light/Low reasoning for quick edits
tips.tip: Most quick UI instructions are easy, so start with Light or Low reasoning. For something more nuanced, like designing an animation, switch to High, then go back to Low.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Keep verification out of the quick loop
tips.tip: For small visual edits, tell Codex to focus on the code changes while you check the result in the browser yourself. Once you're happy, ask it to write the relevant tests and run the additional checks.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Use the same loop for slides, documents and spreadsheets
tips.tip: Instead of asking for a full deck, go one slide at a time and give feedback; for documents, give feedback passage by passage as you read. Ultrafast suits tasks that rely mostly on the model's intelligence and need little validation between changes: slides, documents, spreadsheets, and computer-use tasks made of quick actions.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: When Ultrafast helps less
tips.tip: Faster token generation doesn't make the whole task 4.5× faster: if most of a turn is spent waiting on a build, test suite, compiler, other tool calls or image generation, the speedup is smaller. For well-defined tasks that need lots of experimentation and validation, or that you're happy to leave running overnight, the extra speed matters less.

tips.author: dkundel
tips.title: Try service_tier ultrafast where model time dominates
tips.tip: In the API, compare time spent waiting on the model versus waiting on tools. Good candidates: summaries and Q&A over a document already in context, fast tool calls and computer use (e.g. form filling, ideally with a code mode that writes a script to fill several fields at once), and voice experiences as a backend model alongside GPT-Live-1. Set service_tier to ultrafast and measure time to result. For GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol the promotional rate is 3× Standard through February 28, 2027 (6× from March 1).

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Space is on Plus, with mobile editing
tips.tip: Plus users can now use Space to collaborate with others alongside ChatGPT on interactive pages, slides and sites, and ChatGPT can keep them updated for you. Pages can now be edited on mobile.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: See what keeps a page updated: the clock icon
tips.tip: In a Space page, click the clock icon in the top bar to open Scheduled tasks ("ChatGPT can keep this page updated for you"). The demo shows hourly tasks such as auto-updating a to-do list and refreshing a checklist from Slack.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Mention a dot in the page chat to restructure a page
tips.tip: Use the page's chat sidebar to ask for layout changes. The demo prompt: "@Sara's dot Remove all the long text (put it under in text) and make this more visual", which put an interactive chart up front with sliders below and moved the explanation under the visual.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Restyle a whole page with one prompt
tips.tip: Open the floating prompt box over a page and ask for a page-wide restyle. The demo: "@ChatGPT Make the guidelines feel like an extension of our new website. Use the same typography, colors, and imagery." turned a brand-guidelines page into the new theme in one step.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Share a page with specific people and roles
tips.tip: Click Share in the top right, add people by name, pick their access level (for example Viewer), then click Share.

tips.author: romainhuet
tips.title: Call your dot from Apple CarPlay
tips.tip: You can call your dot from Apple CarPlay and work with it by voice while driving. In the demo Romain asks it about tomorrow's talk (it pulls up the calendar invite) and has it update a demo and docs, test them, and open one draft PR tagging two colleagues for review.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Agents API now supports Daybreak access
tips.tip: The Agents API supports Daybreak access, making it easier to build long-running security agents. Early use cases listed: investigating suspicious activity, implementing new security updates, verifying security fixes, and triaging investigations for human review.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: See a transcript after a Dots call
tips.tip: When a Dots call ends, you can now see a transcript of the call.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Run GPT-6.2 models in Codex, or borrow its system prompt
tips.tip: GPT-6.2 models are tougher to steer through the system prompt, and the Codex team worked hard on that. For the best experience use them directly in Codex; if you run them in another harness such as pi, take passages from the Codex system prompt.

tips.author: _samirism
tips.title: Open your dot from the new app home
tips.tip: In the latest ChatGPT app your dot has its own home: tap the center icon in the bottom bar to open it, then connect apps such as Gmail from the cards in the dot chat. Asked where to find it, @_samirism pointed to Settings > New ChatGPT design.

tips.author: _samirism
tips.title: Connect your dot to Apple Health or medical records
tips.tip: Through Health, your dot can connect to your Apple Health data or medical records, so it can do things like adjust your race training or remind you to book a physical.

tips.author: _samirism
tips.title: Turn on travel mode when abroad
tips.tip: Dots now have a travel mode, so you can keep using your dot when you're abroad.

tips.author: _samirism
tips.title: Share photos to your dot from Google Photos (Android)
tips.tip: On Android you can share photos straight from Google Photos to your dot. The same update improved cloud computer stability and made messages load faster when you open your dot.

tips.author: ChatGPT
tips.title: Give the new Chat-tab Sol detailed instructions
tips.tip: The version of GPT-6.2 Sol rolling out in the Chat tab is tuned for everyday conversation and handles complex requests much better, especially when you give it detailed instructions or ask it to find information online.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: GPT-5.6 retires Dec 23, except in Daybreak Blue
tips.tip: On December 23, GPT-5.6 Sol is deprecated in Chat, and GPT-5.6 Sol and Terra in Work and Codex. GPT-5.6 Sol stays available after that date through Daybreak Blue, where OpenAI is also adding more models, such as GPT-6 Astra in alpha.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Have Astra build editable tools, not finished scenes
tips.tip: Instead of having Astra generate whole scenes (USDA files or full Blender models), use it to build procedural tools inside the engine: here, PCG graphs and supporting Blueprints for roads, platforms, stairs, buildings and walls in Unreal Engine. You can then reshape a walkway or raise a terrace by hand and play the change right away, without another prompt or import pass.
tips.credit: Article by Quentin Marmier (Epic Games) on @UnrealEngine, shared by @pvncher

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Iterate on a vector map, then let the tools build it
tips.tip: Have Astra turn a reference into spatial rules (roads winding uphill, buildings on terraces, stairs linking heights) and draw a vector map of the layout. Iterating on that map is much faster than editing the complex procedural setup directly; the same tool collection then rebuilds the layout with terrain and connections still editable.
tips.credit: Article by Quentin Marmier (Epic Games) on @UnrealEngine, shared by @pvncher

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Ask Astra for more than you think it can do
tips.tip: The author's parting advice: he was at first not demanding enough of Astra and now relies on it more and more for technical work and problem-solving, including complex procedural materials. TL;DR: give it more to do than you think it can.
tips.credit: Article by Quentin Marmier (Epic Games) on @UnrealEngine, shared by @pvncher

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Have your dot triage a feedback channel and brief you each morning
tips.tip: In the demo, the dot watches a Slack feedback channel, tags each piece of feedback and flags duplicates of existing tickets. Custom instructions tell it to send a formatted morning summary that groups items under headings like Bugs and Feature requests, so the day's work is easy to scan.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Delegate Codex work to your dot by voice from your phone
tips.tip: Talk to your dot from your phone and hand it the work: ask for a read-only investigation of some tickets, mockups for feature requests, or a local Codex thread that uses computer use in the signed-in browser on your connected Mac to reproduce a bug. The dot writes the Codex prompt itself, and the new thread is marked "Sent from dot".

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Fan out Codex Cloud threads and PRs, then let the dot report back
tips.tip: Ask the dot to spawn one Codex Cloud thread per issue, each opening its own PR (five threads and five PRs in the demo). Because the threads run in the cloud you can close your laptop; ask the dot to remind you about the PRs when they're done and send an overall status, or progress updates as they run.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Turn a reference image into an editable SVG or 3D model
tips.tip: Enable the SVG & 3D Design plugin in Codex. Codex generates a reference image from your description, then uses it to build an editable SVG or Blender scene. Example prompts on the plugin page: "Create an editable SVG app icon for a birdwatching journal, with a matching PNG preview" and "Rebuild this illustration as an editable SVG and compare the result with the reference." The video also turns a photo of a tarsier into a 3D .glb model.

tips.author: pvncher
tips.title: Ask for design changes in plain language
tips.tip: You don't need to know SVG or Blender to edit the result: tell Codex what to change, as in "Actually let's move the moon to the right side of the marsupial pirate ship and make it crescent shaped." A small change to the SVG code can also add interaction, like a character's eyes following your cursor. Codex can use Blender to check a 3D model from another angle.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Commit a threat model and link it in Codex Cloud settings
tips.tip: Generate a threat model with the $codex-security:threat-model skill (or just type $threat-model in Codex), covering entry points and untrusted inputs, sensitive data paths and privileged actions. Commit it as docs/security/threat-model.md and link it in the Codex Cloud settings for the repo; without one, Codex regenerates a threat model for every security review. Revisit it when entry points, trust boundaries or privileged operations change.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Seed SECURITY.md with the define-security-policy skill
tips.tip: AGENTS.md holds shared engineering instructions, the threat model describes the system's security reality, and SECURITY.md tells Codex how to evaluate and report against it. Run $codex-security:define-security-policy with your key policies to generate SECURITY.md, with sections such as security invariants, reportable findings, severity context (e.g. cross-tenant access is Critical) and out of scope.

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Pass architecture docs to CLI scans as a knowledge base
tips.tip: The Codex Security CLI takes supporting documents for a scan: npx @openai/codex-security scan . --knowledge-base docs/security/payment-service-context.md. Diff scans of local changes or a branch review only the proposed changes and write report.md, scan-manifest.json, findings.json (severity, confidence, locations, remediation) and coverage.json (what was reviewed, excluded or deferred).

tips.author: TheRealAdamG
tips.title: Tune PR Security Review thresholds and path overrides
tips.tip: Turn on Security Review for GitHub PRs at chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/code-review. Automatic reviews post only High and Critical findings by default, while manually requested reviews also post Medium. Add path overrides in the repo's Codex Cloud settings to lower the threshold for sensitive paths such as auth, payments, CI workflows or infrastructure. Start with one workflow (local, PR or CLI) and expand once its findings prove useful.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Estimate agent cost as price x tokens per attempt x attempts
tips.tip: The sticker price per million tokens is only one part of what a model costs you. Multiply it by the tokens the model uses per attempt and the number of attempts it needs (Cost = P x Q x N). Also count the time cost: when you delegate and multitask, your attention is scarce, so features in the Codex app like Appshots and dictation help you stay in the flow while the agent works.

tips.author: danshipper
tips.title: Use your dot as a real-time communication coach
tips.tip: @bran_don_gell had his OpenAI dot, which already read his Slack messages, also review his recorded meetings (via a connected meeting recorder), with simple instructions: communicate more executively, lead with curiosity, and give feedback as close to real time as possible. When he slipped up, the dot pointed it out and he could edit the message or clarify what he'd said. He shared the skill he used, to connect to Slack/Teams plus meeting notes.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Pick the right voice-agent architecture: cascade, turn-based or full duplex
tips.tip: Three ways to build a voice agent: a cascade (transcribe, reason, speak) gives you control but can add delay; turn-based speech-to-speech (GPT-Realtime) takes turns, so an interruption can cut a reply short and reasoning takes time; full duplex (GPT-Live) has no fixed turns and listens while it speaks, so it can hand reasoning to a backend without stalling the conversation.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Delegate GPT-Live reasoning with session.delegation
tips.tip: GPT-Live can hand reasoning off to a backend in three ways, set with session.delegation: type "responses" runs a frontier model (GPT-6.2 Astra is named) through the Responses API with built-in tools such as web and file search; type "client" connects your own model or agent; type "decisions" (Decisions API) has OpenAI pick a tool while your app runs it.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Use standby mode for always-on WebRTC voice agents
tips.tip: For an always-on agent on WebRTC voice, standby mode drops the rate from $0.05/min active to $0.02/min (60% less), and the agent resumes when you speak.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Add GPT-Live to your app with the OpenAI Developers plugin in Codex
tips.tip: To start an integration, open Codex, select the OpenAI Developers plugin and prompt it with something like "Add GPT-Live-1.1 to my booking agent".

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Set up Codex Cloud environments so tasks run without your laptop
tips.tip: Create a Codex Cloud environment for each repo (or use the default environment when no repo is needed). Then you can fire off Codex tasks straight from your phone, or have your dot fire them off, without keeping your laptop open.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Add your dot to Slack group DMs and forward it requests
tips.tip: Add your dot to Slack and group DMs so it can handle tasks there; for example, when someone asks whether you're free for a meeting, forward the message to your dot and let it handle it.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Let your dot use Codex and ChatGPT as tools
tips.tip: Give your dot ChatGPT and Codex as tools: it can start a ChatGPT chat or a Codex task and then manage or babysit it for you.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Use custom instructions to have your dot chase missing details
tips.tip: Write custom instructions for routine operations; for example, when an email arrives missing information, the dot automatically drafts a reply asking the sender to furnish the missing details.

tips.author: gabrielchua
tips.title: Hand repetitive clicking to computer use
tips.tip: If you find yourself clicking many buttons here and there to do the same task, automate it with computer use.
